full_name: Statistics Canada 2021 Census of Population -- Population and dwelling counts (PID 98-10-0002)

features.definition: Total population, 2021 Census (100% data). Verified against the real downloaded 98100002.csv: Canada total 36,991,981, Ontario 14,223,942, City of Toronto 2,794,356 -- all match StatCan's own published 2021 Census figures. DA-level rows come from the companion cube PID 98-10-0015 (98100002 stops at CSD level), same '...Population, 2021 [1]' column under a '(5)' variable-count label instead of '(13)'. Dissemination-block rows come from the 2021 Geographic Attribute File (catalogue 92-151-X, column DBPOP2021_IDPOP2021) -- verified live 2026-08-22: block-level sums reproduce the DA-level PID 98-10-0015 totals exactly for all 3,743 real Toronto DAs.

codes: StatCan 98-10-0459 jobs by workplace CSD (usual place of work)
features.definition: Real workplace-located jobs count -- Canada's analog to the USA's LODES WAC total-jobs field (see pycensus.countries.canada.constants.WORKPLACE_JOBS_PID's docstring for the full live verification). Census-subdivision level, all of Canada (not Ontario-only). Sourced from PID 98-10-0459 ('Commuting flow from geography of residence to geography of work'), summed over every residence CSD for each workplace CSD. Live-verified 2026-08-23: Toronto (CSDUID 3520005) = 753,185; Montreal (2466023) = 649,595; Calgary (4806016) = 370,125; Ottawa (3506008) = 272,920; national sum 10,680,335 is within ~1.5% of the companion table 98-10-0456's own published national 'Usual place of work' total (10,846,770), consistent with StatCan's routine small-cell random rounding. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this measure EXCLUDES workers who worked from home or had no fixed workplace address (a large share in the pandemic-affected 2021 Census), so it materially UNDER-counts true total jobs-by-workplace compared to a complete LODES-style jobs census -- do not treat as directly comparable to usa_lodes_wac_jobsTotal without accounting for this gap.
